key_insight: Semantically related tasks should be clustered before joint training so cooperative multi-task learning becomes constructive instead of causing negative transfer.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical recipe for improving multi-task semantic communication systems by grouping compatible tasks and training only within those groups to boost accuracy and stability.
method: Run a short initial training phase to extract task representations.
Apply hierarchical density-based clustering to discover semantically aligned task groups.
Perform end-to-end cooperative training only inside each cluster.
evidence_signal: Simulations in the abstract show improved accuracy versus both unclustered multi-tasking and individual-task training, with reduced destructive cooperation.
watch_item: The approach depends on a reliable early semantic representation and clustering step, so poor initial embeddings or unstable cluster assignments could hurt downstream performance.
paper_title: Semantic-Aware Task Clustering for Constructive and Cooperative Multi-Tasking
